title: Rahul — Fraud Investigation Agent walkthrough
description: End-to-end tour of the FraudOS — AEGIS.AI fraud detection platform. Walks Rahul's seven screens: home desktop, AI fraud detection dashboard, flagged transaction review queue, transaction description (read-only), compliance reports, model performance, and threshold configuration.

meta.author: Rahul
meta.targetAudience: Fraud investigators, compliance reviewers, model risk leads
meta.pacingNote: Pauses kept short. Real-time fraud data refreshes continuously, so each screen has visible activity in the Live Activity feed and the dashboard chart.

steps.description: Opening line — no UI action, set the stage.

speak.before: Hi, I'm Rahul. Let me walk you through what's happening across our fraud detection platform today.

steps.description: Frame the Live Activity feed on the home screen.

speak.before: We start on the FraudOS home. On the right is the Live Activity feed.
speak.after: Every detection and clearance lands here in real time.

steps.description: Open the AI Fraud Detection Dashboard from the taskbar dock.

speak.before: Let's open the Dashboard.
speak.after: This is the real-time KPI view for today.

steps.description: Frame the dashboard hero banner with agent code and model badges.

speak.before: Banner up top with the agent code and active model badges.
speak.after: Isolation Forest, LSTM, and Azure OpenAI are all online.

steps.description: Frame the four KPI tile row.

speak.before: Four KPI tiles — each one summarises a different angle on today's fraud activity.

steps.description: Total transactions in DB tile.

speak.before: First, total transactions in the database.
speak.after: Live count from Aiven PostgreSQL.

steps.description: Total flagged tile.

speak.before: Flagged transactions.
speak.after: Anything the ensemble model scored above 0.80.

steps.description: Confirmed fraud tile.

speak.before: Confirmed fraud.
speak.after: Investigator-confirmed cases for today.

steps.description: False positive rate tile with target.

speak.before: False positive rate.
speak.after: Target is below thirty percent.

steps.description: Flagged Transactions Over Time chart.

speak.before: Flagged transactions over the last twenty-four hours.
speak.after: Purple is flagged, red is confirmed fraud.

steps.description: Risk Distribution donut by anomaly score band.

speak.before: Risk Distribution donut.
speak.after: Critical, High, Medium, and Low bands by anomaly score.

steps.description: Flagged transactions table on the dashboard.

speak.before: Below the charts, every flagged transaction with model scores and current status.
speak.after: Each row carries the full context the investigator needs.

steps.description: Switch to the Flagged Transaction Review Queue.

speak.before: Let's open the review queue.
speak.after: This is where I confirm or clear each flagged transaction.

steps.description: Filter toolbar at the top of the queue.

speak.before: Filter row up top — search, model, score band, and status.
speak.after: I narrow the queue before working through it.

steps.description: Status dropdown to focus on unreviewed transactions.

speak.before: Filtering by status to focus on what's still unreviewed.

steps.description: Frame the queue table.

speak.before: Each row has the AI explanation and per-model scores.
speak.after: Action buttons on the right — Fraud, Clear, Escalate.

steps.description: Confirm fraud on the highest-confidence row.

speak.before: Top row — critical wire transfer from a new device.
speak.during: Ensemble score above 0.95, AI explanation flags new device and new country.
speak.after: Confirming as fraud. Live Activity logs the decision instantly.

steps.description: Clear a borderline row as a false positive.

speak.before: Next row — investigator context says this one is legitimate.
speak.after: Clearing as a false positive. Feeds back into the retraining loop.

steps.description: Switch to the read-only Transaction Description view.

speak.before: Description page.
speak.after: Same data as the queue but read-only — for stakeholder review.

steps.description: Frame the description table (no Actions column).

speak.before: All flagged transactions in inspection mode.
speak.after: No Fraud, Clear, or Escalate buttons — by design, so demos can't accidentally action a row.

steps.description: Switch to the Compliance Reports screen.

speak.before: Compliance Reports.
speak.after: Today's report up top, archive below.

steps.description: Today's compliance metrics card.

speak.before: Six metrics for today — processed, flagged, fraud, FP rate, review completion, and LLM helpful rate.
speak.after: Auto-generated and delivered to compliance, head of fraud, and the CCO.

steps.description: Download today's compliance PDF.

speak.before: Downloading today's compliance report.
speak.after: Saved as evidence.

steps.description: Frame the report archive table.

speak.before: Below, the historical archive — every prior daily report.
speak.after: Each row has a download button for that date.

steps.description: Switch to the Model Performance Panel.

speak.before: Model performance.
speak.after: Three model cards, FP trend chart, and the audit log.

steps.description: Frame the three model performance cards.

speak.before: Three models — Isolation Forest, LSTM, and the Ensemble.
speak.after: Precision, Recall, F1, and FP Rate for each.

steps.description: Spotlight the Ensemble card — the leading model.

speak.before: Ensemble is the production model.
speak.after: Highest F1 score and lowest FP rate of the three.

steps.description: Weekly FP rate trend chart with target line.

speak.before: Eight-week false positive trend.
speak.after: Descending toward the thirty percent target.

steps.description: Frame the investigator audit log table.

speak.before: Below, the full audit log of investigator decisions.
speak.after: Every action with TX reference, score, and timestamp — append-only and BR-006 compliant.

steps.description: Switch to the Threshold Configuration Panel.

speak.before: Last screen — Threshold Configuration.
speak.after: Where I approve proposed model threshold changes.

steps.description: Validate Admin Role Active badge before approving.

speak.before: Admin Role Active — required before any approval.
speak.after: Without this badge, every Approve button is disabled.

steps.description: Frame the threshold configuration table.

speak.before: Five categories — current and proposed values, with FP and recall impact for each.

steps.description: Approve a pending threshold change within tolerance.

speak.before: First pending row — recall impact within tolerance.
speak.during: FP impact down ten percent, recall impact under one percent.
speak.after: Approved. Submitted to the BR-002 weekly cycle.

steps.description: Spotlight an auto-blocked row that breaches the recall floor.

speak.before: This row is auto-blocked by the system.
speak.after: Recall impact below the ninety-five percent floor — Constraint 3 prevents approval. I do not override.

steps.description: Read the rules footnote at the bottom of the panel.

speak.before: Rules footnote — every change needs Head of Fraud and Risk sign-off.
speak.after: All changes are stored in Aiven PostgreSQL.

steps.description: Back to the home desktop to close the tour.

speak.before: Coming back to the home desktop.
speak.after: Notes and Calendar utilities live here for investigator use.

steps.description: Open Notes modal as a utility example.

speak.before: Single-click opens the Notes modal.
speak.after: For ad-hoc investigation notes that persist across sessions.

steps.description: Close the Notes modal.

speak.before: Closing the modal.

steps.description: Open Calendar modal as the second utility.

speak.before: And the Calendar — for case follow-ups and scheduled reviews.
speak.after: Same single-click pattern.

steps.description: Close the Calendar modal.

speak.before: Closing the modal.

steps.description: Closing line — no UI action.

speak.before: That's the full picture — dashboard, queue, description, reports, model performance, thresholds, and the desktop utilities. Anything you'd like me to dig into?
